source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Dashboard"
And also enter "Server Health" -> "Sensor Reading"

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Sensor Reading & Threshold is human reable and match with spec.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sensor get 'TEMP_MB_CPU0_IN, TEMP_MB_CPU1_IN' 2>&1; echo ---SDR-FALLBACK---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sdr elist 2>&1 | head -100
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: returns FULL raw `ipmitool (OOB lanplus) sensor get "<SENSOR>"` reading + threshold; user judges (read-only).

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES passes the comma-separated pair as one quoted `sensor get` name, so it may query no real record. It does not prove separate CPU0/CPU1 inlet identities, physical locations, socket population, airflow context, thresholds, UI mapping or complete evidence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires separate queries and board/socket mapping. V3.1 further distinguishes motherboard inlet air from CPU package temperature, makes the acceptance population-aware and rejects similarity between the two readings as identity proof.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 874/2291 accepts the invalid-looking single operand and output presence without separate records, physical inlet/socket mapping, operating context, freshness or UI/spec correlation.

original_test_intent: Verify the two distinct motherboard CPU-inlet temperature sensors, `TEMP_MB_CPU0_IN` and `TEMP_MB_CPU1_IN`, are individually readable in Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading and that each has the correct physical identity, value, units, status and supported thresholds for the platform specification.
original_method: Resolve and read the two sensor records separately, map each motherboard inlet sensing point to its physical CPU airflow path and unchanged WebUI row, and compare complete passive fields with the approved per-inlet specification under a recorded fan/load/airflow state. Preserve logs and settings.
manual_activity: The platform owner identifies the two physical inlet sensing points, their CPU/socket association and acceptable values under the specified airflow state. Automation can read both records and UI rows separately; a human resolves label/location or absent-socket ambiguity and owns the verdict. No heat or CPU-load stimulus is authorized.
required_inputs: Exact chassis/board/BMC/BIOS/CPU population and airflow topology, including the physical locations and socket association of CPU0_IN and CPU1_IN
Stable SDR name/number/type/entity/instance and Dashboard/Server Health row for each inlet sensor
Per-inlet expected Celsius scaling/rounding, tolerance, threshold capability/values/hysteresis, health and unavailable semantics
Recorded inlet/room ambient reference location, fan mode/speeds, CPU load/power state, timestamp alignment and allowed update lag/delta
Validated ipmitool/API/browser versions, supported transport/cipher and protected authentication
Pinned immutable accessible `sensor.git` revision/checksum with safety review, or approved manual collection method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL or system logs; pre-existing thermal, fan and CPU events are relevant context and clearing is unnecessary for this passive display case.
Do not send `'TEMP_MB_CPU0_IN, TEMP_MB_CPU1_IN'` as one sensor name unless the vendor explicitly defines it. Query the two stable records independently and preserve two return statuses.
Do not confuse motherboard inlet-air readings with CPU die/package telemetry. Map each physical sensing point and airflow path; closeness between values does not establish correct CPU0/CPU1 identity.
Do not add CPU stress, obstruct airflow, change fan policy or modify thresholds. Record the naturally occurring operating state, since the case does not authorize dynamic thermal response testing.
Use each SDR capability mask when assessing thresholds; do not fail an unsupported limit or accept a missing required one. Treat an unpopulated CPU path only according to the approved configuration.

Do not truncate fallback inventory, expose passwords with `-P`, assume cipher 17 or execute the unavailable internal Script before review. Stop without automatic retry on duplicate/swapped sensors, stale readings or UI/OOB disagreement.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target identity, CPU population, board airflow topology, client and Script; establish a two-row inlet-sensor expectation matrix before querying.
Retrieve CPU0_IN and CPU1_IN independently with full SDR identity, reading, units, supported thresholds, status and timestamp, plus each corresponding unchanged Dashboard and Server Health row.

Compare each physical inlet independently with its specification and approved time-aligned ambient/reference under recorded fan/load conditions; report missing, swapped, duplicate, absent-path or stale behavior separately.
Preserve raw/redacted evidence and logs; perform no clear, load/heat stimulus, threshold/fan change, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve CPU population and the physical CPU0_IN/CPU1_IN sensor-to-socket/airflow mapping.
Provide per-inlet threshold, tolerance, reference, operating-state and freshness acceptance, and approve the Script/tool.
Review the two results separately and issue the verdict without substituting a CPU package sensor or one inlet for the other.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unfit as written unless the vendor has a literal sensor containing the comma: `ipmitool sensor get` normally expects one sensor ID, while the quoted pair can fail as one name. The truncated fallback, credential exposure and absent topology/UI/spec checks also prevent complete coverage.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Enumerate the complete sensor repository, resolve the exact CPU0_IN and CPU1_IN records and retrieve each separately through protected read-only access, then correlate both Dashboard and Server Health rows with the board airflow map.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Both source names, Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading, readability/specification Criteria, generic clear text, Script URL, DeepSeek command and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; the Review layer corrects execution interpretation without editing Master or adding thermal load.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a two-row matrix keyed by physical motherboard inlet location and stable sensor identity, collect each raw/API and UI record at the same passive operating state, and compare per-inlet thresholds/status/value with the versioned Project specification.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact board, CPU population, cooling configuration, BMC/SDR and WebUI build documented by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/board, CPU population, BIOS/BMC/SDR/WebUI, fan policy, management client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Board sensor placement/airflow diagram, CPU-inlet SDR definition, platform thermal limits, WebUI schema and Project configuration specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Executes the two names as separate identities, binds them to physical inlet paths and supplies operating-state, freshness and complete UI/raw evidence without adding active stimulation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Passive inlet readings do not validate CPU package temperature, sensor accuracy across range, load response, alarms, fan control or protection actions; similarity between the two inlets is not cross-coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Socket/airflow/sensor map, per-inlet acceptance matrix, fan/load/ambient timing rules, protected tool or reviewed Script and evidence contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Socket labels may differ among board, BMC and OS; inlet sensors can be physically offset, absent on an unpopulated path, rounded or delayed relative to ambient and CPU telemetry.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish/OEM or calibrated inlet reference telemetry as an approved alternate/corroboration only with the original ipmitool path preserved, interface/version and reason recorded, engineer approval and proof of separate CPU0_IN/CPU1_IN identity, value, threshold, status and freshness equivalence. CPU package temperature is not automatically equivalent.
expected_evidence: Chassis/board/BMC/BIOS identity, CPU population and physical CPU0_IN/CPU1_IN sensing-point plus airflow/socket map
Separate complete raw records with stable IDs, readings, units, threshold capabilities/values, status and timestamps
Separate redacted Dashboard and Server Health evidence mapped to each inlet rather than one combined query
Per-inlet specification and recorded ambient, fan mode/speeds and CPU load/power state with tolerance/update-lag comparison
Explicit missing, absent-path, duplicate, swapped, stale or UI/OOB-disagreement disposition and pinned Script/tool security evidence
No-clear/no-write/no-stress/no-retry proof, final BMC/thermal health, limitations and engineer-owned per-inlet verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The comma-separated Items unambiguously name two inlet sensors even though DeepSeek turned the list into an invalid-looking single operand. Items, UI Procedure and Criteria align; exact mapping and expected values are readiness inputs rather than a core source contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The two-sensor passive validation purpose is clear. Separate names, board mapping and acceptance data can be supplied by the Project, so the case is PACKAGE rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes YES to PACKAGE and replaces the single comma-containing operand with two independently accepted sensor records and UI mappings.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on the hybrid classification while strengthening physical inlet-versus-package semantics, socket-population handling and the rule that similar readings do not prove identity.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-presence reasoning with syntax correction, physical mapping and separate threshold/status/freshness evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No prior invalid draft exists for this sequence.

review_improvement: Prevents a failed one-name query, a CPU package value or one inlet reading from being reported as two motherboard inlet sensors, and makes passive comparison meaningful by recording airflow, fan and load context.
independent_technical_reasoning: The two labels describe motherboard inlet sensing points, not CPU internal temperatures. `sensor get` must resolve each identity separately, and cross-layer CPU numbering cannot be assumed. Inlet values depend on sensor placement and airflow, so physical mapping and contemporaneous fan/load/ambient state are necessary, while this static row provides no authority for a thermal stimulus.
